chief_complaint: Uncontrolled hypertension in the setting of obesity, prediabetes, chronic musculoskeletal pain, and social barriers to care.
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 57‑year‑old woman with a long‑standing history of obesity (diagnosed 1986) and essential hypertension diagnosed in 2018. Despite being on low‑dose lisinopril, recent vital signs show stage 2 hypertension (143/105 mmHg). She has prediabetes (A1c 5.9%) identified in 2008, chronic low‑back pain and knee osteoarthritis for which she takes naproxen sodium, and anemia of unclear etiology. Stress was documented in 2020 and she reports ongoing transport difficulties and limited access to reliable transportation, which may affect medication adherence and follow‑up. She is currently employed full‑time but has a history of intermittent employment. Preventive care visits have been limited, with no recent lipid panel, renal function, or iron studies available.
past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include prior unemployment, part‑time employment, full‑time employment (resolved 2018), limited social contact (resolved 2017), gingivitis and gingival disease (resolved 2018‑2019), primary dental caries (resolved 2018), streptococcal sore throat (resolved 2018), and medication review reminders (resolved 2019‑2020).

active_medications.name: naproxen sodium 220 MG Oral Tablet
active_medications.purpose: Osteoarthritis of knee / chronic musculoskeletal pain

social_determinants: Patient reports ongoing transport problems and lack of reliable transportation, which limit access to care and medication pick‑up. Currently employed full‑time, has higher education, and experiences chronic stress. Prior limited social contact has resolved.
risk_factor_summary: Stage 2 hypertension (SBP 143/DBP 105), obesity (BMI ≥30), prediabetes (A1c 5.9%), anemia, chronic musculoskeletal pain, and chronic NSAID use place the patient at high cardiovascular risk, elevated renal risk, and increased metabolic risk. Charlson comorbidity index is 1, clinical complexity moderate. Comorbidity flags: hypertension, anemia, osteoarthritis. Missing lipid panel, eGFR, and BMI data limit precise risk calculation.

data_quality_flags.issue: BMI value missing despite documented obesity.
Renal function not recorded; important given hypertension and NSAID use.
Lipid panel absent; needed for ASCVD risk assessment.
